doc.title: Jack Lesberg interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997

title: Working 52nd Street at the Famous Door
summary: He worked 52nd Street with Teagarden, Kaminsky, Peanuts Hucko and Cliff Leeman, with Billie Holiday and Ella nearby, an era that will not return.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Yeah, Ray. I went up to work on 52nd Street and I played with Teagarden and Maxie and Peanuts Hucko and Cliff Leeman, whose wife is here. And Louis came in and sat in and played with us at The Famous Door. That’s where I was working. But 52nd Street was just full of those places you know. Billie Holiday was singing on one corner and you’d just walk down the street or cut over and stand across the street and hear who you wanted to hear from the other place. Yeah it was really a kick, 52nd Street. You’ll never see that again.
Yeah some of us were born in the wrong era I think.
When you walk down 52nd Street today, I go by those, the block that they were in and I say oh it’s too bad.
Oh, yeah. Well at least you got to experience it, to be part of it.

Yeah. But those were the people. Let’s see, Ella walking down the street going to work singing some of the tunes as she’s walking along that are running through her head, and just having a good time. It was quite exciting days, everybody going to those wonderful little bars around the corner and so forth.
